title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is working out the closed strata \hat M_G of the boundary stratification of \bar M_{g,ν} indexed by stable ('MD') graphs G, together with the quotients by the graph automorphism groups (the D's). He is now on the one-dimensional cases, as preparation for his study of the 'structure at infinity' (tangential base points, Teichmüller tower).

(i) End of the D_0 discussion. The previous page shows that \hat M_{D_0} ≅ P^1_Z with 'signature' 2 along the section T=2. The map is T ↦ T+1/T from M_{G_0}, a twisted G_m with S_{J'} ≅ Z/2 acting by inversion. Here he places the two boundary points: P_0 goes to the section ∞ and P_1 to the section 2.

(ii) The genus-1 case (88): \hat M_{D_1} ≅ \hat M_{G_1} ≅ \bar M_{1,1} ≅ P^1_Z (j-line) with orbifold 'signatures' 4 and 6 along the sections j=0 and j=J_1=2^α3^β. In modern terms this is the coarse j-line with stacky points of automorphism orders 6 at j=0 and 4 at j=1728=2^6·3^3; he leaves the exponents unwritten and notes J_1 corresponds to the curve with automorphism group Z/4. He also marks something at ∞ (presumably generic ±1, signature 2). A small stratification picture is drawn in the margin.

(iii) Methodological remark: he needs to understand M_{1,1} and \bar M_{1,1} better, starting transcendentally (complex analytic), with the real structure made explicit, i.e. how complex conjugation acts. He postpones this ('J'y reviendrai plus loin').

(iv) Proposition: if dim M_G ≥ 2, the boundary \hat M_G^∞ = \hat M_G \ M_G is geometrically connected, fibre by fibre over Spec Z.

Proof begun here and finished on the next page:
- (89) the stratum closure decomposes as a product over the vertices α∈S of (rigidified, '!') moduli spaces \hat M^!_{g_α,ν_α}, and the open stratum likewise.
- The boundary of a product of connected spaces is connected as soon as at least two factors have positive dimension (each such factor has nonempty boundary).
- This reduces to \bar M_{g,ν} with N = 3g-3+ν ≥ 2. There one chains boundary divisors through pairwise nonempty intersections, using the list (90) of one-edge graphs (irreducible self-node; separating node with stability conditions).
errors: (88): '4 et 6 le long des sections 0 et J_1', read as 'respectively', inverts the correspondence. j=0 has Aut Z/6 (order 6) and j=1728 has Aut Z/4 (order 4); his own parenthesis correctly attaches Z/4 to J_1.

Over Spec Z the 'signatures' are not uniform along the sections. In characteristics 2 and 3, j=0=1728 and the automorphism groups jump to orders 24 and 12, so describing \bar M_{1,1} as P^1_Z with constant signatures 4 and 6 along two disjoint sections is wrong at p=2,3 (the sections 0 and 1728 meet there).

(89) second line: the open stratum M_G should be the product of the open moduli M^!_{g_α,ν_α}; the hat appears to be a slip. Also, without rigidification the stratum is a quotient of the product by Aut(G), so the iso holds only for the '!' (rigidified) versions.
In the proposition statement 'M_C^∞' should read \hat M_G^∞.

ideas.what: \bar M_{1,1} over Z as the j-line P^1 with orbifold points of order 6 at j=0, 4 at j=1728, and a cusp at ∞
ideas.modern_name: moduli stack \bar{\mathcal M}_{1,1} (weighted projective stack P(4,6) over Z[1/6])
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower in low dimension, without this explicit description

ideas.what: Need to study the real structure / complex conjugation on M_{1,1} as a step toward the Galois action at infinity
ideas.modern_name: real structure and complex conjugation in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of M_{1,1}, M_{0,4} and the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Closed boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n} are (up to finite quotient) products of vertex moduli spaces
ideas.modern_name: gluing/clutching morphisms and the stratification by stable graphs

ideas.what: Boundary of \bar M_{g,n} (and of each stratum closure of dim ≥ 2) is geometrically connected fibre by fibre over Z, proved by chaining boundary divisors
ideas.modern_name: connectedness of the boundary / of the boundary complex Δ_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; boundary complex studied by Harer, Chan–Galatius–Payne

deep.surprise_reason: Standard facts about \bar M_{1,1} and the connectedness of the boundary of \bar M_{g,n}. The remark about real structure and complex conjugation is the known program of Esquisse d'un programme; nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'avec rigidifications[?]' should read 'avec signatures' (the same word as in (87)).
'J_1 = 2^α 3^β' is as written: exponents left unspecified, intended 1728 = 2^6·3^3.
The struck line '[-dans les deux derniers iso, on \hat M_{D_1}-]' is correctly marked as cancelled.
In the Proposition, the word written above the struck 'connexe' appears to be 'géom.', i.e. 'est géom. connexe (fibre par fibre)'.
'M_C^∞' in the manuscript should be read as \hat M_G^∞ (the C is a G).
